reason: PIT verification coverage is insufficient; source availability timestamps are required before OOS/model adoption.

weaknesses: Point-in-time verification coverage is 0 of 42,547 acquired rows, so the temporal validity of the data cannot be assessed.
Source availability timestamps are missing or insufficient, preventing confirmation that each feature was available before the relevant match or prediction time.
The supplied metrics contain no verified out-of-sample performance measures, such as calibration, log loss, Brier score, or accuracy.
The pipeline is explicitly blocked, so model results cannot currently be interpreted as reliable OOS evidence.
candidate_experiments: Add source-availability timestamps and prediction-cutoff timestamps to every feature record, then measure the proportion of rows that pass point-in-time validation.
Build a historical replay test that reconstructs the exact information set available before each match and reports valid, invalid, and unverifiable rows.
Audit timestamp provenance for each data source, including timezone handling, publication delays, revisions, and backfills.
Create a leakage test suite using intentionally shifted or future-only features to verify that the validation process detects temporal contamination.
After PIT coverage is established, evaluate time-based OOS splits with pre-specified metrics and confidence intervals, separately reporting results by league, season, and data availability.
risks: Potential look-ahead bias or target leakage cannot be ruled out because no rows are PIT verified.
Backfilled, revised, or retrospectively corrected source data may make historical inputs appear more complete or timely than they were in real time.
The 42,547 acquired rows may not represent the subset that would have been available at prediction time, creating unknown selection and coverage bias.
Timezone, publication-delay, and event-ordering errors could misclassify future information as available information.
Any apparent model performance derived before resolving the verification gap would be difficult to reproduce or trust.
The current evidence is insufficient to support model or OOS adoption.
